title: Object Pose Estimation with Statistical Guarantees: Conformal Keypoint Detection and Geometric Uncertainty Propagation

en.text: Estimating an object's 6D pose (its three-dimensional rotation and translation relative to the camera) is a workhorse of augmented reality, autonomous driving, robotic manipulation, and space robotics. The dominant recipe is a two-stage pipeline: a neural network first detects semantic keypoints on the image, then a geometric solver recovers the pose by minimizing reprojection error through Perspective-n-Points (PnP). This pipeline tops standard benchmarks, but it hands back a single pose with no statement about how much to trust it.

For a demo that is a minor inconvenience. For a self-driving car or a robot arm it is a real problem. The pipeline gives no guarantee that the detected keypoints are close to the truth, no guarantee that the optimizer found the right pose rather than a plausible wrong one, and no formal bound on the worst-case error between the estimate and the groundtruth. A system that must act on a pose would like to know not just the estimate, but how far off it could possibly be.

This paper, from Heng Yang and Marco Pavone at NVIDIA Research and presented at CVPR 2023, closes that gap. It keeps the familiar two-stage structure and injects two ingredients: conformal keypoint detection, which turns heuristic heatmap detections into prediction sets that provably cover the true keypoints with a user-chosen probability, and geometric uncertainty propagation, which pushes those sets through the geometry to a set of poses that covers the true pose with the same probability. The result is, to the authors' knowledge, the first object pose estimator that attaches a provable and computable worst-case error bound to its output.

en.caption: Figure 1. The full pipeline. From (a) an input image and its keypoint heatmaps, conformal prediction produces (b) circular or elliptical prediction sets that cover the true keypoints with a chosen probability (e.g. 90%). Propagating these sets through the pose geometry yields (c) the Pose UnceRtainty SEt (PURSE), which contains the true pose with the same probability. RANSAG samples PURSE to produce (d) an average pose, and a semidefinite (SDP) relaxation computes (e) the worst-case rotation and translation error bounds (blue duck: worst rotation; red duck: worst translation).

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12246    |    Code: https://github.com/NVlabs/ConformalKeypoint
The gap: accurate on average, silent about the worst case

The authors name three challenges that stand between a two-stage pipeline and a trustworthy pose. First, keypoints from a neural network can be arbitrarily wrong: an occluded or ambiguous part produces an outlier detection far from the true location. Second, the geometric stage must reject those outliers, which is a nonconvex optimization; fast heuristics like RANSAC are the standard tool but cannot certify that they found the global optimum, and they can fail silently. Third, and most fundamentally, none of this delivers provably correct uncertainty quantification: there is no formal, probabilistic bound on the error between the estimate and the groundtruth. Recent work could certify that the optimization reached its global optimum, which helps with the second challenge, but a certified optimizer still does not tell you how close the resulting pose is to the truth.
Conformal keypoint detection: from heatmaps to prediction sets

The first ingredient replaces a point detection with a set that comes with a coverage guarantee. The tool is inductive conformal prediction. The authors set aside a calibration set of labeled images and, for each one, compute a nonconformity score that measures how surprised the detector is by the true keypoint. Sorting these scores gives a threshold: any new detection is expanded into the set of pixels whose score falls under that threshold. The guarantee is clean and distribution-free: for a target error rate epsilon, the true keypoint lies inside its prediction set with probability at least 1 minus epsilon (90% at epsilon = 0.1), as long as calibration and test images are exchangeable.

The shape of the set depends on how the score is defined. A peak design measures the scaled distance between the true keypoint and the heatmap's single most probable pixel, producing a circular set (a ball). A covariance design measures a Mahalanobis distance over the top detections, producing an elliptical set that can stretch along the direction the detector is least sure about. Circular sets are simpler; elliptical sets adapt to anisotropic uncertainty and, as the experiments show, usually cover at least as well.
Geometric uncertainty propagation: from keypoint sets to a set of poses

A guarantee on keypoints is only useful if it survives the trip to the pose. Each keypoint prediction set becomes a constraint on the 6D pose: the pose must reproject the three-dimensional model point into that keypoint's set. Intersecting all these constraints defines the Pose UnceRtainty SEt, or PURSE, the set of all poses consistent with every keypoint's prediction set. Because each keypoint is covered with probability 1 minus epsilon, PURSE contains the true pose with the same probability. The catch is that PURSE is a nonconvex subset of SE(3), so you cannot simply read a point estimate or an error bar off it.

The paper extracts two things from PURSE. To get a usable point estimate, RANdom SAmple averaGing (RANSAG) repeatedly samples three keypoints, solves the minimal P3P problem, keeps the poses that fall inside PURSE, and averages the accepted rotations and translations into an average pose. To get an error bound, the authors ask a worst-case question: over all poses still inside PURSE, how far can one get from the average pose? That maximization is nonconvex, but it admits a semidefinite (SDP) relaxation whose solution is either exact or a valid upper bound. Whenever PURSE actually contains the true pose (which happens with probability 1 minus epsilon), that number is a certified worst-case bound on the rotation and translation error.
Does the guarantee hold in practice?

The experiments run on LineMOD Occlusion (LM-O), a challenging benchmark of 1214 test images showing 8 objects on a table under heavy occlusion. The 200 images selected by the BOP challenge serve as the calibration set that conformal prediction needs, and all 1214 are used for testing. The authors evaluate four setups that cross two choices: keypoints from groundtruth bounding boxes or from a Faster-RCNN detector, and prediction sets that are balls or ellipses.

The first thing to check is coverage: does a target of 90% actually deliver 90%? Conformal prediction guarantees this in expectation over calibration sets, but any single calibration set gives a slightly random coverage. Figure 2 shows how that randomness shrinks as the calibration set grows.

en.caption: Figure 2. Distribution of the achieved coverage at a 90% target (epsilon = 0.1) for different calibration-set sizes n. Even at n = 200 the distribution centers on 0.9; as n grows to 1000 and 5000 it concentrates tightly around the target, so a larger calibration set makes the realized coverage more reliable.

en.text: The takeaway is that even the modest 200-image calibration set available on LM-O is enough to center the coverage on the target, and more calibration data mainly tightens the spread.
Coverage also has to hold object by object, not just on average, otherwise a strong overall number could be hiding a failure on one hard category.

en.caption: Figure 3. Empirical coverage per LM-O object under the four setups (gt-ball, gt-ellipse, frcnn-ball, frcnn-ellipse). Across all 8 objects the conformalized prediction sets sit at or above the 90% target, confirming valid coverage in practice.

en.text: Every object clears the 90% line under every setup, so the coverage guarantee is not an average that hides failures on hard objects. The bounds themselves behave as promised too: in the paper's scatter plots of certified bound against actual error, every case where PURSE covers the true pose stays below the diagonal, meaning the bound is never smaller than the real error when the guarantee holds.
Accuracy: the guarantee is not paid for with worse poses

A guarantee would be a poor trade if it wrecked accuracy. It does not. Judged by the 2D-projection metric (a pose counts as correct if its mean reprojection error is under 5 pixels), the average pose from PURSE matches or beats strong baselines. With groundtruth bounding boxes and elliptical sets it reaches 70.6% mean success, ahead of PVNet, the strongest baseline, at 61.1%. With Faster-RCNN detections the numbers are close to PVNet rather than ahead, which the authors report plainly.

en.caption: Table 1. Mean 2D-projection success rate on LM-O (a pose is correct if the mean reprojection error is below 5 pixels). Our average pose is shown at epsilon = 0.1.

en.text: Two knobs shape this trade-off. The error rate epsilon acts as a dial: a smaller epsilon (0.1) gives larger, more conservative prediction sets and stronger coverage, while a larger epsilon (0.4) shrinks the sets, raises the average pose's success rate, and lowers coverage. And elliptical sets, built from the covariance design, generally match or beat circular ones, which is why gt-ellipse leads the table.
What it means, and where it stops

The lasting message is that a standard two-stage pose estimator can be upgraded into one that reports how wrong it might be, with a genuine statistical guarantee, and at little or no cost in accuracy. Conformal prediction supplies coverage on the keypoints, geometry carries that coverage to the pose as PURSE, and semidefinite relaxation turns the set into concrete worst-case bounds. Because the wrapper sits on top of any heatmap-based keypoint detector, it is largely detector-agnostic.

The honest boundaries are worth stating. The coverage guarantee rests on exchangeability between calibration and test data, which holds on LM-O because poses were sampled roughly uniformly but would need care in a streaming or strongly correlated setting. The worst-case bounds are correct but can be conservative, sometimes much larger than the actual error, and the paper studies ways to tighten them. And the guarantee is on the keypoints and the resulting set, not a promise that any single point estimate is within a fixed distance. Even with those caveats, the framework points toward provably correct perception for other geometric vision problems where safety, not just benchmark score, is what matters.

zh.text: 估计一个物体的 6D 位姿（相对相机的三维旋转与平移）是增强现实、自动驾驶、机器人操作、空间机器人等系统的基础能力。目前主流做法是两阶段流程（two-stage pipeline）：先用神经网络在图像上检测语义关键点（semantic keypoints），再用几何求解器通过 Perspective-n-Points（PnP）最小化重投影误差，反解出位姿。这个流程在各类基准上成绩领先，但它只会给出一个位姿，却不告诉你这个结果有多可信。
对一个 demo 来说，这点无所谓；但对自动驾驶或机械臂而言，这是个真问题。流程无法保证检测到的关键点接近真值，无法保证优化器找到的是正确位姿而不是一个「看起来对」的错误解，也无法给出估计与真值之间最坏误差的形式化上界。一个要依据位姿去行动的系统，真正想知道的不只是「估计值是多少」，还有「它最坏可能偏多少」。

这篇来自 NVIDIA Research 的 Heng Yang 与 Marco Pavone、发表于 CVPR 2023 的工作，正是要补上这个缺口。它保留了熟悉的两阶段结构，只注入两个部件：conformal 关键点检测，把启发式的热力图（heatmap）检测变成能以用户指定概率覆盖真实关键点的预测集合（prediction set）；以及几何不确定性传播，把这些集合沿几何关系传播到位姿，得到一个以同样概率覆盖真实位姿的集合。据作者所知，这是第一个能为输出附上可证明、可计算最坏误差界的物体位姿估计器。

zh.caption: 图1 完整流程。从（a）输入图像及其关键点热力图出发，conformal prediction 生成（b）以指定概率（如 90%）覆盖真实关键点的圆形或椭圆形预测集合；将这些集合沿位姿几何传播，得到（c）以同样概率包含真实位姿的位姿不确定性集合（PURSE）；RANSAG 从 PURSE 中采样得到（d）平均位姿，再由半定松弛（semidefinite relaxation）计算（e）最坏旋转与平移误差界（蓝鸭：最坏旋转；红鸭：最坏平移）。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12246    ｜    代码：https://github.com/NVlabs/ConformalKeypoint
问题：平均很准，最坏情况却说不清

作者点出两阶段流程通往「可信位姿」的三个挑战。其一，神经网络给出的关键点可能任意偏离真值：遮挡或语义模糊的部位会产生远离真实位置的离群检测（outlier）。其二，几何阶段必须剔除这些离群点，而这是一个非凸优化问题；RANSAC 之类的快速启发式是标准工具，却无法保证找到的是全局最优，还可能「无声地」失败。其三，也是最根本的一点，上述环节都无法提供可证明正确的不确定性量化：估计与真值之间没有形式化的概率误差界。近期有工作能证明优化确实达到了全局最优，缓解了第二个挑战，但一个「被认证的优化器」仍然不会告诉你，最终位姿离真值到底有多近。
Conformal 关键点检测：从热力图到预测集合

第一个部件把「一个点的检测」替换成「一个带覆盖保证的集合」，用的工具是归纳式 conformal 预测（inductive conformal prediction）。作者留出一个带标注的校准集（calibration set），对每张图计算一个非一致性分数（nonconformity score），衡量检测器对真实关键点有多「意外」。把这些分数排序就得到一个阈值：任何新的检测都会被扩展成「分数低于该阈值的所有像素」组成的集合。这个保证干净且与分布无关：对给定的错误率 epsilon，真实关键点落在其预测集合内的概率至少为 1 减 epsilon（epsilon=0.1 时即 90%），前提是校准图像与测试图像可交换（exchangeable）。
集合的形状取决于分数怎么定义。峰值（peak）设计衡量真实关键点与热力图最可能像素之间的缩放距离，得到圆形集合（ball）；协方差（covariance）设计在若干最强检测上衡量马氏距离（Mahalanobis distance），得到椭圆形集合，可沿检测器最不确定的方向拉伸。圆形集合更简单，椭圆形集合能适应各向异性的不确定性，实验中其覆盖通常不逊于甚至更好。
几何不确定性传播：从关键点集合到位姿集合

关键点上的保证，只有在传到位姿后仍然成立才有价值。每个关键点预测集合都转化为对 6D 位姿的一个约束：该位姿必须把对应的三维模型点重投影到这个关键点的集合内。把所有约束相交，就定义出位姿不确定性集合（Pose UnceRtainty SEt，PURSE），即与每个关键点预测集合都一致的全部位姿。由于每个关键点都以 1 减 epsilon 的概率被覆盖，PURSE 也以同样概率包含真实位姿。难点在于 PURSE 是 SE(3) 上的非凸集合，无法直接从中读出点估计或误差棒。

论文从 PURSE 中提取两样东西。为得到可用的点估计，随机采样平均（RANdom SAmple averaGing，RANSAG）反复采样三个关键点、求解最小的 P3P 问题、保留落在 PURSE 内的位姿，再把这些位姿的旋转与平移平均成一个平均位姿（average pose）。为得到误差界，作者提出一个最坏情况问题：在仍属于 PURSE 的所有位姿中，离平均位姿最远能有多远？这个最大化是非凸的，但可以做半定松弛（SDP relaxation），其解要么精确、要么是一个有效上界。只要 PURSE 确实包含真实位姿（以 1 减 epsilon 概率发生），这个数值就是对旋转与平移误差的认证最坏界。
保证在实际中站得住吗？
实验在 LineMOD Occlusion（LM-O）上进行，这是一个有挑战性的基准，包含 1214 张测试图，展示桌面上 8 类物体在严重遮挡下的情形。BOP 挑战选出的 200 张图作为 conformal 预测所需的校准集，全部 1214 张用于测试。作者评估四种设置，交叉两个选择：关键点来自真值边界框还是 Faster-RCNN 检测器，预测集合是圆形还是椭圆形。
首先要检验覆盖率：目标 90% 是否真的兑现 90%？conformal 预测保证的是在校准集上的期望覆盖，而任何单个校准集给出的覆盖都带一点随机性。图2 展示了这种随机性如何随校准集增大而收窄。

zh.caption: 图2 目标 90%（epsilon=0.1）下，不同校准集规模 n 所达到覆盖率的分布。即使 n=200，分布也已经以 0.9 为中心；随着 n 增至 1000、5000，分布向目标紧紧收拢，说明更大的校准集让实际覆盖更可靠。

zh.text: 结论是：即便 LM-O 上只有 200 张校准图，也足以把覆盖率的中心压在目标上；更多校准数据主要是收紧分布的宽度。
覆盖率还必须逐个物体成立，而不仅是平均成立，否则一个漂亮的总体数字可能正掩盖着某个困难类别上的失败。

zh.caption: 图3 四种设置（gt-ball、gt-ellipse、frcnn-ball、frcnn-ellipse）下每类 LM-O 物体的经验覆盖率。8 类物体在所有设置下都达到或超过 90% 目标，验证了实际中的覆盖有效性。

zh.text: 每类物体在每种设置下都越过 90% 线，说明覆盖保证并不是一个掩盖了困难物体失败的平均值。误差界本身也如约成立：在论文中「认证界 vs 实际误差」的散点图里，凡是 PURSE 覆盖真实位姿的点都落在对角线下方，意味着在保证成立时，界从不小于真实误差。
精度：保证不是用更差的位姿换来的
如果一个保证要以牺牲精度为代价，那就得不偿失，但这里并没有。按 2D 投影指标衡量（平均重投影误差小于 5 像素即算正确），从 PURSE 得到的平均位姿与强基线持平或更好。在真值边界框加椭圆集合下，它达到 70.6% 的平均成功率，高于最强基线 PVNet 的 61.1%。而在 Faster-RCNN 检测下，数字与 PVNet 接近而非领先，作者对此如实报告。

zh.caption: 表1 LM-O 上的平均 2D 投影成功率（平均重投影误差小于 5 像素即算正确）。本文平均位姿取 epsilon=0.1。

zh.text: 有两个旋钮在塑造这个取舍。错误率 epsilon 像一个刻度盘：更小的 epsilon（0.1）给出更大、更保守的预测集合与更强覆盖；更大的 epsilon（0.4）收缩集合、提高平均位姿成功率、降低覆盖。而由协方差设计得到的椭圆集合通常与圆形持平或更好，这也是 gt-ellipse 在表中领先的原因。
它意味着什么，又止步于何处
这项工作留下的核心信息是：一个标准的两阶段位姿估计器，可以被升级成「会告诉你自己可能错多少」的估计器，且带着真正的统计保证，几乎不损失精度。conformal 预测在关键点上提供覆盖，几何把这份覆盖传播到位姿形成 PURSE，半定松弛再把集合转成具体的最坏误差界。由于这层「外壳」套在任意基于热力图的关键点检测器之上，它在很大程度上与具体检测器无关。

边界同样值得如实说明。覆盖保证依赖校准数据与测试数据的可交换性，这在 LM-O 上成立（位姿大致均匀采样），但在流式或强相关的场景中需要谨慎。最坏误差界是正确的，却可能偏保守，有时远大于实际误差，论文也研究了收紧它的方法。此外，保证是针对关键点及由此得到的集合，而不是承诺某个单一点估计一定落在固定距离内。即便有这些前提，这一框架仍指向一个方向：为那些「安全比刷分更重要」的几何视觉问题，提供可证明正确的感知。

en.title: CVPR 2023 | A Pose Estimator That Tells You How Wrong It Might Be

zh.subtitle: NVIDIA Research 在标准两阶段流程中加入 conformal 关键点检测与几何不确定性传播，首次为物体位姿估计给出可证明、可计算的最坏误差界。

en.caption: Figure 1. The full pipeline. From (a) an input image and its keypoint heatmaps, conformal prediction produces (b) circular or elliptical prediction sets that cover the true keypoints with a chosen probability (e.g. 90%). Propagating these sets through the pose geometry yields (c) the Pose UnceRtainty SEt (PURSE), which contains the true pose with the same probability. RANSAG samples PURSE to produce (d) an average pose, and a semidefinite (SDP) relaxation computes (e) the worst-case rotation and translation error bounds (blue duck: worst rotation; red duck: worst translation).

en.text: The gap: accurate on average, silent about the worst case

The authors name three challenges that stand between a two-stage pipeline and a trustworthy pose. First, keypoints from a neural network can be arbitrarily wrong: an occluded or ambiguous part produces an outlier detection far from the true location. Second, the geometric stage must reject those outliers, which is a nonconvex optimization; fast heuristics like RANSAC are the standard tool but cannot certify that they found the global optimum, and they can fail silently. Third, and most fundamentally, none of this delivers provably correct uncertainty quantification: there is no formal, probabilistic bound on the error between the estimate and the groundtruth. Recent work could certify that the optimization reached its global optimum, which helps with the second challenge, but a certified optimizer still does not tell you how close the resulting pose is to the truth.

zh.caption: 图1 完整流程。从（a）输入图像及其关键点热力图出发，conformal prediction 生成（b）以指定概率（如 90%）覆盖真实关键点的圆形或椭圆形预测集合；将这些集合沿位姿几何传播，得到（c）以同样概率包含真实位姿的位姿不确定性集合（PURSE）；RANSAG 从 PURSE 中采样得到（d）平均位姿，再由半定松弛（semidefinite relaxation）计算（e）最坏旋转与平移误差界（蓝鸭：最坏旋转；红鸭：最坏平移）。

zh.text: 问题：平均很准，最坏情况却说不清

作者点出两阶段流程通往「可信位姿」的三个挑战。其一，神经网络给出的关键点可能任意偏离真值：遮挡或语义模糊的部位会产生远离真实位置的离群检测（outlier）。其二，几何阶段必须剔除这些离群点，而这是一个非凸优化问题；RANSAC 之类的快速启发式是标准工具，却无法保证找到的是全局最优，还可能「无声地」失败。其三，也是最根本的一点，上述环节都无法提供可证明正确的不确定性量化：估计与真值之间没有形式化的概率误差界。近期有工作能证明优化确实达到了全局最优，缓解了第二个挑战，但一个「被认证的优化器」仍然不会告诉你，最终位姿离真值到底有多近。

zh.subtitle: NVIDIA Research 在标准两阶段流程中加入 conformal 关键点检测与几何不确定性传播，首次为物体位姿估计给出可证明、可计算的最坏误差界。

en.caption: Figure 1. The full pipeline. From (a) an input image and its keypoint heatmaps, conformal prediction produces (b) circular or elliptical prediction sets that cover the true keypoints with a chosen probability (e.g. 90%). Propagating these sets through the pose geometry yields (c) the Pose UnceRtainty SEt (PURSE), which contains the true pose with the same probability. RANSAG samples PURSE to produce (d) an average pose, and a semidefinite (SDP) relaxation computes (e) the worst-case rotation and translation error bounds (blue duck: worst rotation; red duck: worst translation).

en.text: Conformal keypoint detection: from heatmaps to prediction sets

The first ingredient replaces a point detection with a set that comes with a coverage guarantee. The tool is inductive conformal prediction. The authors set aside a calibration set of labeled images and, for each one, compute a nonconformity score that measures how surprised the detector is by the true keypoint. Sorting these scores gives a threshold: any new detection is expanded into the set of pixels whose score falls under that threshold. The guarantee is clean and distribution-free: for a target error rate epsilon, the true keypoint lies inside its prediction set with probability at least 1 minus epsilon (90% at epsilon = 0.1), as long as calibration and test images are exchangeable.

The shape of the set depends on how the score is defined. A peak design measures the scaled distance between the true keypoint and the heatmap's single most probable pixel, producing a circular set (a ball). A covariance design measures a Mahalanobis distance over the top detections, producing an elliptical set that can stretch along the direction the detector is least sure about. Circular sets are simpler; elliptical sets adapt to anisotropic uncertainty and, as the experiments show, usually cover at least as well.

zh.caption: 图1 完整流程。从（a）输入图像及其关键点热力图出发，conformal prediction 生成（b）以指定概率（如 90%）覆盖真实关键点的圆形或椭圆形预测集合；将这些集合沿位姿几何传播，得到（c）以同样概率包含真实位姿的位姿不确定性集合（PURSE）；RANSAG 从 PURSE 中采样得到（d）平均位姿，再由半定松弛（semidefinite relaxation）计算（e）最坏旋转与平移误差界（蓝鸭：最坏旋转；红鸭：最坏平移）。

zh.text: Conformal 关键点检测：从热力图到预测集合

第一个部件把「一个点的检测」替换成「一个带覆盖保证的集合」，用的工具是归纳式 conformal 预测（inductive conformal prediction）。作者留出一个带标注的校准集（calibration set），对每张图计算一个非一致性分数（nonconformity score），衡量检测器对真实关键点有多「意外」。把这些分数排序就得到一个阈值：任何新的检测都会被扩展成「分数低于该阈值的所有像素」组成的集合。这个保证干净且与分布无关：对给定的错误率 epsilon，真实关键点落在其预测集合内的概率至少为 1 减 epsilon（epsilon=0.1 时即 90%），前提是校准图像与测试图像可交换（exchangeable）。
集合的形状取决于分数怎么定义。峰值（peak）设计衡量真实关键点与热力图最可能像素之间的缩放距离，得到圆形集合（ball）；协方差（covariance）设计在若干最强检测上衡量马氏距离（Mahalanobis distance），得到椭圆形集合，可沿检测器最不确定的方向拉伸。圆形集合更简单，椭圆形集合能适应各向异性的不确定性，实验中其覆盖通常不逊于甚至更好。

zh.subtitle: NVIDIA Research 在标准两阶段流程中加入 conformal 关键点检测与几何不确定性传播，首次为物体位姿估计给出可证明、可计算的最坏误差界。

en.caption: Figure 1. The full pipeline. From (a) an input image and its keypoint heatmaps, conformal prediction produces (b) circular or elliptical prediction sets that cover the true keypoints with a chosen probability (e.g. 90%). Propagating these sets through the pose geometry yields (c) the Pose UnceRtainty SEt (PURSE), which contains the true pose with the same probability. RANSAG samples PURSE to produce (d) an average pose, and a semidefinite (SDP) relaxation computes (e) the worst-case rotation and translation error bounds (blue duck: worst rotation; red duck: worst translation).

en.text: Accuracy: the guarantee is not paid for with worse poses

A guarantee would be a poor trade if it wrecked accuracy. It does not. Judged by the 2D-projection metric (a pose counts as correct if its mean reprojection error is under 5 pixels), the average pose from PURSE matches or beats strong baselines. With groundtruth bounding boxes and elliptical sets it reaches 70.6% mean success, ahead of PVNet, the strongest baseline, at 61.1%. With Faster-RCNN detections the numbers are close to PVNet rather than ahead, which the authors report plainly.

en.caption: Table 1. Mean 2D-projection success rate on LM-O (a pose is correct if the mean reprojection error is below 5 pixels). Our average pose is shown at epsilon = 0.1.

en.text: Two knobs shape this trade-off. The error rate epsilon acts as a dial: a smaller epsilon (0.1) gives larger, more conservative prediction sets and stronger coverage, while a larger epsilon (0.4) shrinks the sets, raises the average pose's success rate, and lowers coverage. And elliptical sets, built from the covariance design, generally match or beat circular ones, which is why gt-ellipse leads the table.

zh.caption: 图1 完整流程。从（a）输入图像及其关键点热力图出发，conformal prediction 生成（b）以指定概率（如 90%）覆盖真实关键点的圆形或椭圆形预测集合；将这些集合沿位姿几何传播，得到（c）以同样概率包含真实位姿的位姿不确定性集合（PURSE）；RANSAG 从 PURSE 中采样得到（d）平均位姿，再由半定松弛（semidefinite relaxation）计算（e）最坏旋转与平移误差界（蓝鸭：最坏旋转；红鸭：最坏平移）。

zh.text: 精度：保证不是用更差的位姿换来的
如果一个保证要以牺牲精度为代价，那就得不偿失，但这里并没有。按 2D 投影指标衡量（平均重投影误差小于 5 像素即算正确），从 PURSE 得到的平均位姿与强基线持平或更好。在真值边界框加椭圆集合下，它达到 70.6% 的平均成功率，高于最强基线 PVNet 的 61.1%。而在 Faster-RCNN 检测下，数字与 PVNet 接近而非领先，作者对此如实报告。

zh.caption: 表1 LM-O 上的平均 2D 投影成功率（平均重投影误差小于 5 像素即算正确）。本文平均位姿取 epsilon=0.1。

zh.text: 有两个旋钮在塑造这个取舍。错误率 epsilon 像一个刻度盘：更小的 epsilon（0.1）给出更大、更保守的预测集合与更强覆盖；更大的 epsilon（0.4）收缩集合、提高平均位姿成功率、降低覆盖。而由协方差设计得到的椭圆集合通常与圆形持平或更好，这也是 gt-ellipse 在表中领先的原因。
它意味着什么，又止步于何处
这项工作留下的核心信息是：一个标准的两阶段位姿估计器，可以被升级成「会告诉你自己可能错多少」的估计器，且带着真正的统计保证，几乎不损失精度。conformal 预测在关键点上提供覆盖，几何把这份覆盖传播到位姿形成 PURSE，半定松弛再把集合转成具体的最坏误差界。由于这层「外壳」套在任意基于热力图的关键点检测器之上，它在很大程度上与具体检测器无关。

边界同样值得如实说明。覆盖保证依赖校准数据与测试数据的可交换性，这在 LM-O 上成立（位姿大致均匀采样），但在流式或强相关的场景中需要谨慎。最坏误差界是正确的，却可能偏保守，有时远大于实际误差，论文也研究了收紧它的方法。此外，保证是针对关键点及由此得到的集合，而不是承诺某个单一点估计一定落在固定距离内。即便有这些前提，这一框架仍指向一个方向：为那些「安全比刷分更重要」的几何视觉问题，提供可证明正确的感知。

The lasting message is that a standard two-stage pose estimator can be upgraded into one that reports how wrong it might be, with a genuine statistical guarantee, and at little or no cost in accuracy. Even with those caveats, the framework points toward provably correct perception for other geometric vision problems where safety, not just benchmark score, is what matters.

zh.text: 估计一个物体的 6D 位姿（相对相机的三维旋转与平移）是增强现实、自动驾驶、机器人操作、空间机器人等系统的基础能力。目前主流做法是两阶段流程（two-stage pipeline）：先用神经网络在图像上检测语义关键点（semantic keypoints），再用几何求解器通过 Perspective-n-Points（PnP）最小化重投影误差，反解出位姿。这个流程在各类基准上成绩领先，但它只会给出一个位姿，却不告诉你这个结果有多可信。
对一个 demo 来说，这点无所谓；但对自动驾驶或机械臂而言，这是个真问题。流程无法保证检测到的关键点接近真值，无法保证优化器找到的是正确位姿而不是一个「看起来对」的错误解，也无法给出估计与真值之间最坏误差的形式化上界。一个要依据位姿去行动的系统，真正想知道的不只是「估计值是多少」，还有「它最坏可能偏多少」。

这篇来自 NVIDIA Research 的 Heng Yang 与 Marco Pavone、发表于 CVPR 2023 的工作，正是要补上这个缺口。它保留了熟悉的两阶段结构，只注入两个部件：conformal 关键点检测，把启发式的热力图（heatmap）检测变成能以用户指定概率覆盖真实关键点的预测集合（prediction set）；以及几何不确定性传播，把这些集合沿几何关系传播到位姿，得到一个以同样概率覆盖真实位姿的集合。据作者所知，这是第一个能为输出附上可证明、可计算最坏误差界的物体位姿估计器。

zh.caption: 图1 完整流程。从（a）输入图像及其关键点热力图出发，conformal prediction 生成（b）以指定概率（如 90%）覆盖真实关键点的圆形或椭圆形预测集合；将这些集合沿位姿几何传播，得到（c）以同样概率包含真实位姿的位姿不确定性集合（PURSE）；RANSAG 从 PURSE 中采样得到（d）平均位姿，再由半定松弛（semidefinite relaxation）计算（e）最坏旋转与平移误差界（蓝鸭：最坏旋转；红鸭：最坏平移）。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12246    ｜    代码：https://github.com/NVlabs/ConformalKeypoint

en.title: CVPR 2023 | A Pose Estimator That Tells You How Wrong It Might Be
en.subtitle: NVIDIA Research adds conformal keypoint detection and geometric uncertainty propagation to the standard two-stage pipeline, producing the first object pose estimate with a provable, computable worst-case error bound.

zh.title: CVPR 2023 | 让位姿估计告诉你「最坏会错多少」
zh.subtitle: NVIDIA Research 在标准两阶段流程中加入 conformal 关键点检测与几何不确定性传播，首次为物体位姿估计给出可证明、可计算的最坏误差界。

en.caption: Figure 1. The full pipeline. From (a) an input image and its keypoint heatmaps, conformal prediction produces (b) circular or elliptical prediction sets that cover the true keypoints with a chosen probability (e.g. 90%). Propagating these sets through the pose geometry yields (c) the Pose UnceRtainty SEt (PURSE), which contains the true pose with the same probability. RANSAG samples PURSE to produce (d) an average pose, and a semidefinite (SDP) relaxation computes (e) the worst-case rotation and translation error bounds (blue duck: worst rotation; red duck: worst translation).

en.text: The gap: accurate on average, silent about the worst case

The authors name three challenges that stand between a two-stage pipeline and a trustworthy pose. First, keypoints from a neural network can be arbitrarily wrong: an occluded or ambiguous part produces an outlier detection far from the true location. Second, the geometric stage must reject those outliers, which is a nonconvex optimization; fast heuristics like RANSAC are the standard tool but cannot certify that they found the global optimum, and they can fail silently. Third, and most fundamentally, none of this delivers provably correct uncertainty quantification: there is no formal, probabilistic bound on the error between the estimate and the groundtruth. Recent work could certify that the optimization reached its global optimum, which helps with the second challenge, but a certified optimizer still does not tell you how close the resulting pose is to the truth.

zh.caption: 图1 完整流程。从（a）输入图像及其关键点热力图出发，conformal prediction 生成（b）以指定概率（如 90%）覆盖真实关键点的圆形或椭圆形预测集合；将这些集合沿位姿几何传播，得到（c）以同样概率包含真实位姿的位姿不确定性集合（PURSE）；RANSAG 从 PURSE 中采样得到（d）平均位姿，再由半定松弛（semidefinite relaxation）计算（e）最坏旋转与平移误差界（蓝鸭：最坏旋转；红鸭：最坏平移）。

zh.text: 它意味着什么，又止步于何处
这项工作留下的核心信息是：一个标准的两阶段位姿估计器，可以被升级成「会告诉你自己可能错多少」的估计器，且带着真正的统计保证，几乎不损失精度。conformal 预测在关键点上提供覆盖，几何把这份覆盖传播到位姿形成 PURSE，半定松弛再把集合转成具体的最坏误差界。由于这层「外壳」套在任意基于热力图的关键点检测器之上，它在很大程度上与具体检测器无关。

边界同样值得如实说明。覆盖保证依赖校准数据与测试数据的可交换性，这在 LM-O 上成立（位姿大致均匀采样），但在流式或强相关的场景中需要谨慎。最坏误差界是正确的，却可能偏保守，有时远大于实际误差，论文也研究了收紧它的方法。此外，保证是针对关键点及由此得到的集合，而不是承诺某个单一点估计一定落在固定距离内。即便有这些前提，这一框架仍指向一个方向：为那些「安全比刷分更重要」的几何视觉问题，提供可证明正确的感知。

en.subtitle: NVIDIA Research adds conformal keypoint detection and geometric uncertainty propagation to the standard two-stage pipeline, producing the first object pose estimate with a provable, computable worst-case error bound.

zh.title: CVPR 2023 | 让位姿估计告诉你「最坏会错多少」
zh.subtitle: NVIDIA Research 在标准两阶段流程中加入 conformal 关键点检测与几何不确定性传播，首次为物体位姿估计给出可证明、可计算的最坏误差界。

en.text: Estimating an object's 6D pose (its three-dimensional rotation and translation relative to the camera) is a workhorse of augmented reality, autonomous driving, robotic manipulation, and space robotics. The dominant recipe is a two-stage pipeline: a neural network first detects semantic keypoints on the image, then a geometric solver recovers the pose by minimizing reprojection error through Perspective-n-Points (PnP). This pipeline tops standard benchmarks, but it hands back a single pose with no statement about how much to trust it.

For a demo that is a minor inconvenience. For a self-driving car or a robot arm it is a real problem. The pipeline gives no guarantee that the detected keypoints are close to the truth, no guarantee that the optimizer found the right pose rather than a plausible wrong one, and no formal bound on the worst-case error between the estimate and the groundtruth. A system that must act on a pose would like to know not just the estimate, but how far off it could possibly be.

This paper, from Heng Yang and Marco Pavone at NVIDIA Research and presented at CVPR 2023, closes that gap. It keeps the familiar two-stage structure and injects two ingredients: conformal keypoint detection, which turns heuristic heatmap detections into prediction sets that provably cover the true keypoints with a user-chosen probability, and geometric uncertainty propagation, which pushes those sets through the geometry to a set of poses that covers the true pose with the same probability. The result is, to the authors' knowledge, the first object pose estimator that attaches a provable and computable worst-case error bound to its output.

en.caption: Figure 1. The full pipeline. From (a) an input image and its keypoint heatmaps, conformal prediction produces (b) circular or elliptical prediction sets that cover the true keypoints with a chosen probability (e.g. 90%). Propagating these sets through the pose geometry yields (c) the Pose UnceRtainty SEt (PURSE), which contains the true pose with the same probability. RANSAG samples PURSE to produce (d) an average pose, and a semidefinite (SDP) relaxation computes (e) the worst-case rotation and translation error bounds (blue duck: worst rotation; red duck: worst translation).

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12246    |    Code: https://github.com/NVlabs/ConformalKeypoint

zh.text: 保证在实际中站得住吗？
实验在 LineMOD Occlusion（LM-O）上进行，这是一个有挑战性的基准，包含 1214 张测试图，展示桌面上 8 类物体在严重遮挡下的情形。BOP 挑战选出的 200 张图作为 conformal 预测所需的校准集，全部 1214 张用于测试。作者评估四种设置，交叉两个选择：关键点来自真值边界框还是 Faster-RCNN 检测器，预测集合是圆形还是椭圆形。
首先要检验覆盖率：目标 90% 是否真的兑现 90%？conformal 预测保证的是在校准集上的期望覆盖，而任何单个校准集给出的覆盖都带一点随机性。图2 展示了这种随机性如何随校准集增大而收窄。

zh.caption: 图2 目标 90%（epsilon=0.1）下，不同校准集规模 n 所达到覆盖率的分布。即使 n=200，分布也已经以 0.9 为中心；随着 n 增至 1000、5000，分布向目标紧紧收拢，说明更大的校准集让实际覆盖更可靠。

zh.text: 结论是：即便 LM-O 上只有 200 张校准图，也足以把覆盖率的中心压在目标上；更多校准数据主要是收紧分布的宽度。
覆盖率还必须逐个物体成立，而不仅是平均成立，否则一个漂亮的总体数字可能正掩盖着某个困难类别上的失败。

zh.caption: 图3 四种设置（gt-ball、gt-ellipse、frcnn-ball、frcnn-ellipse）下每类 LM-O 物体的经验覆盖率。8 类物体在所有设置下都达到或超过 90% 目标，验证了实际中的覆盖有效性。

zh.text: 每类物体在每种设置下都越过 90% 线，说明覆盖保证并不是一个掩盖了困难物体失败的平均值。误差界本身也如约成立：在论文中「认证界 vs 实际误差」的散点图里，凡是 PURSE 覆盖真实位姿的点都落在对角线下方，意味着在保证成立时，界从不小于真实误差。

en.text: Does the guarantee hold in practice?

The experiments run on LineMOD Occlusion (LM-O), a challenging benchmark of 1214 test images showing 8 objects on a table under heavy occlusion. The 200 images selected by the BOP challenge serve as the calibration set that conformal prediction needs, and all 1214 are used for testing. The authors evaluate four setups that cross two choices: keypoints from groundtruth bounding boxes or from a Faster-RCNN detector, and prediction sets that are balls or ellipses.

The first thing to check is coverage: does a target of 90% actually deliver 90%? Conformal prediction guarantees this in expectation over calibration sets, but any single calibration set gives a slightly random coverage. Figure 2 shows how that randomness shrinks as the calibration set grows.

en.caption: Figure 2. Distribution of the achieved coverage at a 90% target (epsilon = 0.1) for different calibration-set sizes n. Even at n = 200 the distribution centers on 0.9; as n grows to 1000 and 5000 it concentrates tightly around the target, so a larger calibration set makes the realized coverage more reliable.

en.text: The takeaway is that even the modest 200-image calibration set available on LM-O is enough to center the coverage on the target, and more calibration data mainly tightens the spread.
Coverage also has to hold object by object, not just on average, otherwise a strong overall number could be hiding a failure on one hard category.

en.caption: Figure 3. Empirical coverage per LM-O object under the four setups (gt-ball, gt-ellipse, frcnn-ball, frcnn-ellipse). Across all 8 objects the conformalized prediction sets sit at or above the 90% target, confirming valid coverage in practice.

en.text: Every object clears the 90% line under every setup, so the coverage guarantee is not an average that hides failures on hard objects. The bounds themselves behave as promised too: in the paper's scatter plots of certified bound against actual error, every case where PURSE covers the true pose stays below the diagonal, meaning the bound is never smaller than the real error when the guarantee holds.
